title: A Design Science Research Methodology for Information Systems Research
problem_statement: The lack of a widely accepted, standardized methodology for conducting and evaluating design science research in Information Systems, leading to uncertainty in research execution and evaluation.
domain: Information Systems and Computer Science Research Methodology
theoretical_framework: Design Science Research (DSR) paradigm and Systems Development Methodology
methodology: Development of a six-stage sequential process model synthesized from prior design science literature and validated through four case study applications across different research entry points.
evaluation: Qualitative evaluation of the methodology across four distinct case studies demonstrating problem-centered, objective-centered, design-and-development-centered, and client-initiated research trajectories.
key_findings: Established a six-step nominal process model for Design Science Research: Problem Identification, Objectives Definition, Design and Development, Demonstration, Evaluation, and Communication.

Demonstrated that DSR can initiate from multiple entry points depending on whether the research originates from an observed problem, an objective opportunity, a technical artifact innovation, or a client need.
Provided a standard structure for rigorous evaluation of computational artifacts against explicit quantitative and qualitative solution objectives.
scope_and_delimitations: Focuses on design-oriented information systems and computational artifact research, excluding purely behavioral survey methods.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt: The process model presented here is not intended to suggest that DSR should always proceed in a rigid, linear fashion. Research processes are often iterative and may cycle through steps.
limitations.summary: The methodology is presented as a nominal linear sequence but inherently requires iterative cycles in practical implementation.

generalizability_gap: Primarily illustrated in information systems research; requires adaptation for specialized deep learning and optimization engineering workflows.
methodological_gap: Does not prescribe domain-specific statistical significance testing protocols for machine learning benchmarks.
future_work: Application and refinement of DSRM across specialized computational, artificial intelligence, and software engineering domains.
